title: Command Policy
description: Whether and how the agency harness may run one command (a tools row) for a model: the shell allowlist, one row per tool. Commands run as argv with no shell - no pipes, redirects, or substitution - so `cd` is the mission working directory, not a command. Options are allowlisted, not denylisted: GNU long-option abbreviation and short-flag bundling defeat denylists. Hazards record why options or whole tools are excluded, citing GTFOBins. Decisions use the rule vocabulary of Claude Code permissions (allow/ask/deny) and Codex rules (allow/prompt/forbidden).

program.description: Executable name when it differs from the tool slug (tool httpie runs `http`); resolved to an absolute path on PATH before running

oneOf.title: Allow - the harness runs it within these rules
Ask - an operator confirms each invocation
Deny - never run for a model (see hazards)

decision.description: Whether the harness may run it at all

subcommands.description: Allowed first operands (git: status, log, ...). Absent: the tool takes none. A subcommand not listed is refused.

flags.description: Allowlisted options, exact tokens (-n, --max-count). Any other option is refused, including abbreviations and bundles.

flags_with_value.description: The subset of flags that take a value (next token, or --flag=value)

max.description: Most operands allowed; null for no limit

expressions.description: Leading operands that are expressions, not paths (grep PATTERN, jq FILTER, date +FORMAT)

paths.description: Remaining operands are paths and must resolve inside the mission working directory (symlinks followed)

inject.description: Arguments placed right after the program, before the model's (git: --no-pager -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.pager=cat)

hazards.description: Why options, operands, or the whole tool are excluded

effect.description: What it would let a model do
